registers.name: CONTROL_0
registers.description: Primary control byte. Writing the enable/launch/clear bits affects request issuance and fault handling. Soft reset is level-sensitive within the synchronous control plane and should be pulsed by firmware.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.description: Master enable for request issuance and closed-loop operation.

fields.name: SOFT_RESET
fields.description: Requests a synchronous soft-reset action in the control plane.

fields.name: LAUNCH
fields.description: Launches one outbound surrogate request when ENABLE is set and outstanding limit allows it. Self-clearing after acceptance behavior is implementation-defined but the request must be issued once per asserted launch event.

fields.name: FAULT_CLEAR
fields.description: Clears transient fault latches according to sticky-fault policy.

fields.name: STICKY_FAULT
fields.description: Retains fault latches until firmware explicitly clears them.

fields.name: PIPELINED_MODE
fields.description: Allows limited multiple outstanding requests when supported by the outstanding limit.

fields.name: SESSION_ROLLOVER
fields.description: Indicates host-managed session rollover; stale detection uses this to invalidate older request context.

fields.name: STATUS_CLEAR
fields.description: Clears latched IRQ/status indications without changing unrelated control state.

registers.name: REQUEST_0
registers.description: Request metadata byte 0. Encodes request type and sequence seed low bits.

fields.name: REQUEST_TYPE
fields.description: 8-bit request type tag placed into the outbound surrogate request word.

registers.name: REQUEST_1
registers.description: Request metadata byte 1. Sequence seed high byte.

fields.name: SEQUENCE_SEED_LSB
fields.description: Low byte of the 16-bit sequence seed used as the initial request sequence basis.

registers.name: REQUEST_2
registers.description: Request metadata byte 2. Sequence seed high byte and compact model identifiers low bits.

fields.name: SEQUENCE_SEED_MSB
fields.description: High byte of the 16-bit sequence seed.

registers.name: REQUEST_3
registers.description: Request metadata byte 3. Operating velocity low byte.

fields.name: OPERATING_VELOCITY_LSB
fields.description: Low byte of the 16-bit representative operating velocity in the supported envelope, e.g. 38.89 m/s encoded by firmware convention.

registers.name: REQUEST_4
registers.description: Request metadata byte 4. Operating velocity high byte.

fields.name: OPERATING_VELOCITY_MSB
fields.description: High byte of the 16-bit operating velocity field.

registers.name: REQUEST_5
registers.description: Request metadata byte 5. Velocity fraction low byte.

fields.name: VELOCITY_FRACTION_LSB
fields.description: Low byte of the 16-bit velocity fraction field used as compact operating-point metadata.

registers.name: REQUEST_6
registers.description: Request metadata byte 6. Velocity fraction high byte.

fields.name: VELOCITY_FRACTION_MSB
fields.description: High byte of the 16-bit velocity fraction field.

registers.name: REQUEST_7
registers.description: Request metadata byte 7. Reference ID low byte.

fields.name: REFERENCE_ID_LSB
fields.description: Low byte of the 16-bit compact reference identifier for DrivAerML or equivalent host-side reference naming.

registers.name: REQUEST_8
registers.description: Request metadata byte 8. Reference ID high byte.

fields.name: REFERENCE_ID_MSB
fields.description: High byte of the 16-bit compact reference identifier.

registers.name: REQUEST_9
registers.description: Request metadata byte 9. Geometry ID low byte.

fields.name: GEOMETRY_ID_LSB
fields.description: Low byte of the compact geometry identifier. No raw geometry payload is stored in RTL.

registers.name: REQUEST_10
registers.description: Request metadata byte 10. Geometry ID high byte.

fields.name: GEOMETRY_ID_MSB
fields.description: High byte of the compact geometry identifier.

registers.name: REQUEST_11
registers.description: Optional compact operating-point metadata byte 11. Reserved for future host metadata within the compact request envelope.

fields.name: RESERVED_REQ_11
fields.description: Reserved for future compact request metadata; firmware should write zero unless a future contract defines use.

registers.name: LIMITS_13

fields.name: STEP_LIMIT_MSB

registers.name: TIMEOUT_0

fields.description: Low byte of the 16-bit timeout threshold in cycles.

registers.name: TIMEOUT_1
registers.description: Timeout threshold high byte.

fields.name: TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD_MSB

registers.name: FRESHNESS_0

registers.name: PIPELINE_0
registers.description: Pipelining and outstanding limit control.

fields.name: OUTSTANDING_LIMIT
fields.description: Maximum number of outstanding requests allowed. Zero may be treated as one outstanding in firmware policy if needed.

fields.name: PIPELINED_MODE
fields.description: Enables limited pipelined operation when set.

fields.name: RESERVED_PIPELINE
fields.description: Reserved.

registers.name: STATUS_POLICY_0
registers.description: IRQ and sticky-fault policy bits.

fields.name: IRQ_ON_ACCEPT
fields.description: If set, accepted responses may generate an interrupt/status event.

fields.name: IRQ_ON_FAULT
fields.description: If set, fault entry may generate an interrupt/status event.

fields.name: IRQ_ON_TIMEOUT
fields.description: If set, timeout events may generate an interrupt/status event.

fields.name: RESERVED_STATUS_POLICY
fields.description: Reserved.

registers.name: STATE_READBACK_0
registers.description: Telemetry byte 0. Current state and busy/idle/flag summary.

fields.name: TELEMETRY_STATE
fields.description: Current controller state encoding from telemetry_status.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.description: Busy flag indicating an outstanding request or active transaction.

fields.name: TIMEOUT_FAULT
fields.description: Timeout fault indication.

fields.name: STALE_FAULT
fields.description: Stale fault indication.

fields.name: PROTOCOL_FAULT
fields.description: Protocol fault indication.

registers.name: STATE_READBACK_1
registers.description: Telemetry byte 1. Clamp/fallback/valid flags.

fields.name: CLAMP_ACTIVE
fields.description: Indicates clamping or step-limiting activity on the accepted command.

fields.name: FALLBACK_ACTIVE
fields.description: Indicates deterministic safe fallback is active.

fields.name: IRQ_LATCHED
fields.description: Interrupt latch indication.

fields.name: RESERVED_STATE_1
fields.description: Reserved.

registers.name: STATUS_OUTSTANDING
registers.description: Outstanding request count and response count low byte summary.

fields.name: OUTSTANDING_COUNT
fields.description: Current outstanding request count.

fields.name: RESPONSE_COUNT_LSB
fields.description: Low 5 bits of the 16-bit response acceptance counter.

registers.name: LAST_SEQ_0
registers.description: Last accepted sequence low byte.

fields.name: LAST_ACCEPTED_SEQ_LSB
fields.description: Low byte of the last accepted sequence number.

registers.name: LAST_SEQ_1
registers.description: Last accepted sequence high byte.

fields.name: LAST_ACCEPTED_SEQ_MSB
fields.description: High byte of the last accepted sequence number.

registers.name: RESPONSE_COUNT_0
registers.description: Response acceptance counter low byte.

fields.name: RESPONSE_COUNT_LSB
fields.description: Low byte of the 16-bit accepted-response counter.

registers.name: RESPONSE_COUNT_1
registers.description: Response acceptance counter high byte.

fields.name: RESPONSE_COUNT_MSB
fields.description: High byte of the 16-bit accepted-response counter.

registers.name: FAULTS_0
registers.description: Fault status summary byte.

fields.name: TIMEOUT_FAULT_LATCHED
fields.description: Latched timeout fault indication.

fields.name: STICKY_FAULT_MODE
fields.description: Reflects sticky-fault configuration state.

fields.name: RESERVED_FAULTS_0
fields.description: Reserved.

registers.name: MMIO_ERROR_STATUS
registers.description: Access error and unsupported-address status.

fields.name: MMIO_ERROR
fields.description: Indicates an unsupported or malformed MMIO access.

fields.name: RESERVED_ERROR
fields.description: Reserved.

sources.name: status_irq
sources.description: Synchronous status/interrupt output asserted or latched according to configuration on response acceptance, timeout, or fault entry.

init_sequence: Hold rst_n low, then release it synchronously.
Program LIMITS_0..LIMITS_13 with safe min/max/fallback/step-limit values; ensure min <= fallback <= max.
Program TIMEOUT_0..TIMEOUT_1 and FRESHNESS_0..FRESHNESS_1 with conservative nonzero thresholds.
Program PIPELINE_0 with the desired outstanding limit and pipelined mode setting.
Program STATUS_POLICY_0 to select IRQ behavior.
Program REQUEST_0..REQUEST_11 with request type, sequence seed, operating velocity around the desired point, velocity fraction, reference identifier, and geometry identifier.
Write CONTROL_0 with ENABLE=1, clear SOFT_RESET if used as a pulse, and leave LAUNCH=0 until ready to issue a request.
polling_sequence: Poll STATE_READBACK_0, STATE_READBACK_1, STATUS_OUTSTANDING, LAST_SEQ_0..LAST_SEQ_1, RESPONSE_COUNT_0..RESPONSE_COUNT_1, and FAULTS_0 until response acceptance or a fault event is observed.
Check MMIO_ERROR_STATUS after accesses to confirm no unsupported address was used.
If no response is seen before timeout, treat TIMEOUT_FAULT_LATCHED or TIMEOUT_FAULT telemetry as a safe-fallback condition.
irq_sequence: Enable IRQ policy bits in STATUS_POLICY_0 as desired.
On status_irq assertion, read FAULTS_0 and telemetry bytes to determine whether the event was acceptance, timeout, or fault entry.
If the IRQ is latched, write CONTROL_0 with STATUS_CLEAR=1 to clear the latched status, then deassert it in a later write if needed.

consistency_notes: All assumptions remain compatible with DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.
The regmap uses a custom byte-addressed register interface description because the top-level MMIO port set is semantic and 64-bit wide; no incompatible AXI/APB protocol is imposed.
Wider semantic fields are split across multiple 8-bit registers to remain compatible with the specified 64-bit register-mapped control/status interface and to avoid inventing wider bus semantics.
No hierarchy, ports, or filenames are altered from DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.
